memo.verdict: PARK, bearish, low conviction on any positive equity outcome. Do not progress to Early-Stage Assessment; authorise no further research spend between prints. The memo's own framing: the change forces are real and dated, and the platform that must survive to collect them is not funded. Two named re-activation triggers, both taken verbatim from the risks family's own re-evaluation trigger: (1) non-dilutive refinancing above SEK 100m, whether from a business-unit divestment, a patent monetisation or a multi-year credit facility; (2) a binding high-volume automotive contract with a major original equipment manufacturer specifying minimum purchase guarantees. A third, softer trigger: a Q2 2026 Autosense print holding at or above SEK 45m, which management guided to and which the earnings-review family calls a falsifiable benchmark; a print materially below SEK 40m collapses the licensing thesis. Kill-adjacent watch item: group cash below SEK 30m at any quarter end moves the recommendation from Park to removal from the universe. The risks family (compact digest generated 2026-07-30, from a 21,570-word source) recommends at §14 "a definitive Kill decision due to an unsustainable liquidity profile and unviable competitive positioning; stage progression hypothesis: Kill". The memo adopts that direction in full and does not overturn it. Park rather than Kill is procedural: the Triaging decision pivot in Procedure 1 offers progress or park only, and Kill is not an available Triaging verdict.
case: The case for the verdict runs in the memo's own order: the change forces are genuine, the base cannot survive to collect them, and the setup fits the two guardrails Viewforth does not underwrite better than any setup it does.

Change forces are real and dated. The exogenous leg is regulatory and specific. EU General Safety Regulation 2019/2144 makes driver drowsiness and advanced driver distraction warning mandatory for all newly registered passenger cars, vans, trucks and buses from 7 July 2026. Euro NCAP confirms compliant driver monitoring contributes up to 25 points toward a five-star rating. The driver-monitoring market scales from under 1m units to roughly 20m units annually by 2026. Tobii holds EU type-approval for its single-camera driver and occupant monitoring system from July 2025, enabling mass production from late 2025, and added UN Regulation 171 type-approval for driver control assistance systems in November 2025. The internal leg is cost execution. SEK 120m of savings over three quarters against a SEK 100m target, SEK 48m in Q1 2026 alone; quarterly operating costs from SEK 246m in Q2 2024 to SEK 126m in Q1 2026; average full-time equivalents 404 against 521 a year earlier; free cash flow positive for a second consecutive quarter.

The base cannot carry them. Cash of SEK 39m against a SEK 25m facility leaves roughly SEK 64m of total liquidity against SEK 526m of interest-bearing liabilities. SEK 95m of deferred COVID tax falls due in Q1 2027, a further SEK 39m in Q3 2027, and the USD 28m Xperi note begins cash amortisation in 2027 secured by a floating lien over core assets. On SEK 39m of cash, the change-forces family's own arithmetic says a 5% revenue miss evaporates the liquidity buffer. Returns have been negative since at least 2016. The base is also being actively disinvested: research recognised in the income statement fell to SEK 337m in 2025 from SEK 589m; quarterly capitalised product development fell to SEK 28m in Q1 2026 from SEK 64m, against the business-foundations family's stated early-warning threshold of SEK 25m.
counter_case: The risks family's own recommendation is Kill, not Park. Its §14 states: "the researcher recommends a definitive Kill decision due to an unsustainable liquidity profile and unviable competitive positioning; stage progression hypothesis: Kill". The memo adopts that direction in full and does not overturn it; the Park verdict is procedural, since Kill is not an available Triaging verdict. Two mitigating facts postdate the bear framing: free cash flow of SEK 57m in Q4 2025 and SEK 17m in Q1 2026, and a quarterly cost base of SEK 126m. Neither changes the answer, because SEK 95m of tax falls due in Q1 2027 against SEK 39m of cash and a SEK 25m facility. The risks family's own stated kill trigger, group cash below SEK 30m, has not fired: the last reported figure is SEK 39m at 31 March 2026. No later-dated Tobii print has run against that trigger, so there is no basis for treating the risks report as stale; the later earnings-review family, dated 2026-08-14, is 18 days newer and corroborates it, adding worse competitor data.
The strongest bull arguments the memo carried, in their strongest form:
triggers: Re-activation trigger one. Non-dilutive refinancing above SEK 100m, from a business-unit divestment, a patent monetisation or a multi-year credit facility. Taken verbatim from the risks family's re-evaluation trigger. This is the single event that could move Element E8 Required Attribute 7.
Re-activation trigger two. A binding high-volume automotive contract with a major original equipment manufacturer specifying minimum purchase guarantees. Also verbatim from the risks family.

Re-activation trigger three. A Q2 2026 Autosense print holding at or above SEK 45m, which management guided to and which the earnings-review family calls a falsifiable benchmark. A print materially below SEK 40m collapses the licensing thesis and would revert Autosense to low-margin non-recurring engineering.
Kill-adjacent watch item. Group cash below SEK 30m at any quarter end moves the recommendation from Park to removal from the universe entirely.

Open question one. Is the Q1 2026 Autosense revenue of SEK 45m recurring royalty or a one-off licence fee? Unproven. It turns on the Q2 2026 print, which the earnings-review family dates to August 2026 and which is not in the source set.

Open question two. Does the EU General Safety Regulation mandate accrue to Tobii specifically? The memo answers no: the mandate compels the function, not the supplier. It turns on whether OEMs standardise on single-camera mirror architectures, where Tobii holds EU homologation from July 2025.
